title: Moten, Alphonso Trent and Troy Floyd as dance bands
summary: Albert says Moten played rags and popular songs, and that Trent and Floyd led the first big bands in Texas. Floyd's players were self-taught, Trent's were schoolmen.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: It's different students of blues. Now, I don't know what... You take Benny Moulton. Was he a blues piano player, or what?
Didn't confine himself to blues. He had a band. No.
He played rags and popular songs, you know.
That's what it was. It's in the era of the first big bands, because the really first good big band to migrate into Texas was Alfonso Trent.
Now, he had a tremendous band. Then behind him, Troy Floyd with his orchestra of gold. Well, there, there weren't blues bands. There were dance bands. Uh-huh.

Well, I listen to Trent, and it's a very good band. I don't know how to say it in words, but you know, solid is the word to me. When a man plays the solid blues, that's something different. Now, Troy Floyd's band could play the solid blues.

Well, he had a different type of musician in his band. Uh-huh. In Troy's band, most of those musicians were self-taught. Uh-huh. And a man that sometimes is self-taught has a better feeling within himself than a musician that's going to school to study nothing but music. Uh-huh. And he's what we call an automatic player. He just plays. Uh-huh. Well, Trent had quite a number of fellas in that band that were schoolmen. They had been to school and had good educations. And this music was just another sideline which became part of their livelihood after they found out that the band was on the top and was doing jobs. Uh-huh.
